title: Chromatic Pipeline Editor with Undo History
description: The user manages a post-processing pipeline applied to a scene containing CesiumMan walking through a corridor of DispersionTest orbs. A sidebar lists available effects (bloom, chromatic aberration, vignette, pixelation, color grading, sepia, film grain) that can be dragged into an ordered pipeline stack. Each effect has coupled intensity and radius sliders that obey an energy conservation rule: total combined intensity across all active effects cannot exceed a budget of 3.0. The user must compose, reorder, tune, and undo/redo pipeline states to match a target visual shown as a thumbnail.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with the EffectComposer from three/addons/postprocessing. Load CesiumMan.glb animated and walking in place at center, and place 5 instances of DispersionTest.glb in a semicircle behind him at radius 3. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,1.5,4) looking at origin. Add ambient light 0.4 and a directional light from (2,4,3) intensity 1.2. Implement 7 post-processing effects as ShaderPass nodes: Bloom, ChromaticAberration, Vignette, Pixelation, ColorGrading (hue-shift), Sepia, and FilmGrain. Render a left sidebar (HTML overlay, 200px wide) showing available effects as draggable cards. Users drag cards into an ordered pipeline stack panel below. Each active effect shows two sliders: intensity (0-1) and radius/spread (0-1). Enforce an energy conservation law: sum of all active effect intensities must not exceed 3.0. If adding or increasing one effect would exceed the budget, proportionally scale down all other active effects to maintain the cap, visually updating their sliders. Effects in the stack can be reordered via drag-and-drop, which changes the EffectComposer pass order and alters the visual result. Double-clicking a card in the stack removes it. Implement full undo/redo with Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y that captures the entire pipeline state (which effects, their order, and all slider values) as snapshots, supporting at least 20 history levels. Show a small target thumbnail in the top-right corner representing a preset pipeline configuration (Bloom 0.7, Vignette 0.5, FilmGrain 0.3 in that order). Display a match percentage comparing current pipeline to target based on effect presence, order, and parameter proximity. Animate CesiumMan using AnimationMixer. The scene should render continuously with the post-processing pipeline updating in real-time as the user modifies it.
